chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

A man came to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) from behind the Balkh river and said: I will ask you a question; if you answer it with what I have (consider correct), I will say with your Imama.
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Ask whatever you wish.
He said: Inform me about your Lord, when was He? And how was He? And upon what thing was His reliance?
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, defined the 'where' without a 'where' and the 'how' without a 'how', and His reliance was on His Power.

The man stood up to him, kissed his head, and said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that Ali is the vicegerent of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the one who took charge after him with what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took charge of, and that you are the truthful Imams, and that you are the successor after them.

key_terms.متى كان: When was He? (referring to temporal existence)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida explain God's timelessness and spacelessness?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights Imam al-Rida’s (peace be upon him) concise theological response to the Mu'tazilite-influenced question of God's spatial and temporal location, affirming divine transcendence (tanzih) beyond human categories of 'where' and 'how'. The man’s subsequent act of kissing the Imam’s head signifies the acceptance of this doctrine as the basis for recognizing the Imams as the rightful successors (al-Qa'im) of the Prophet. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imams' role in preserving and articulating core tenets of Tawhid against contemporary philosophical challenges.
